issues.legal_issue: The Central Empowered Committee may be constituted as a permanent statutory body under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Decisions of the Central and State Governments under the notification constituting the Central Empowered Committee remain subject to the Supreme Court’s orders and directions.
The Central Empowered Committee must adopt and publish guidelines governing its meetings, procedures, site visits, public participation, timelines, and preparation of reports.
Environmental regulatory bodies must have clearly defined compositions, qualifications, tenures, appointment and removal processes, and suitably expert staff.
Environmental regulatory bodies must receive adequate and clearly established funding.
The mandates of environmental regulatory bodies must be clearly demarcated, with arrangements for coordination to prevent overlap and duplication.
Environmental regulatory bodies must make their rules, regulations, guidelines, and procedures for permissions and approvals accessible to the public.
Environmental regulatory bodies must prescribe procedures for public hearings, decision-making, appeals, and decision timelines.
Environmental regulatory bodies must clearly allocate officers’ duties and responsibilities and establish methods for accountability.
Environmental regulatory bodies must undergo regular and systematic audits of their functioning.
Constitutional courts must monitor the institutionalisation and functioning of environmental regulatory bodies and ensure that they have adequate infrastructure and human resources.
